scope: Offline review of saved original firmware only. No hardware access, frozen input edit, runtime hook installation or validation.
decision: A once-started original vapp plus native broker is a plausible smaller prototype than repeated Framework destroy/reentry. A PAN-slot-only hook does not establish ownership. Complete hot switching remains dynamically unproved.

cache_and_pointer_rules.selected_cold_start: Persist the wrappers inside the existing copied A7 image. Original cold loader creates executable code before tasks start; runtime hooks change only ordinary aligned data callback pointers from native task context. No host-injected executable code or live instruction patch is proposed.
cache_and_pointer_rules.publication: Initialize heapctx and save original callbacks before publication. Use compiler-visible ordered atomics/OS synchronization and a DMB when publishing pointers. Preserve Thumb bit1 vs ARM bit0. Atomic aligned pointer store does not provide an ownership or lifecycle acknowledgement.
cache_and_pointer_rules.critical_sections: Serialize admitted submit paths and transition state; do not hold native driver locks across sleeps. Do not disable touch/LCD IRQs or halt GUI tasks to simulate ownership. Multi-core/cache attributes and all participating callbacks still need verification.
cache_and_pointer_rules.range_cache_caution: Thumb0x38002054 is range invalidate: interior lines use MCRp15 c7,c6,1 and only edges use clean+invalidatec7,c14,1. It must not be reused as a general payload clean operation.0x380020f0 is a candidate D-clean range path usingc7,c10,1. Complete runtime executable injection I-cache/alias synchronization remains unqualified and is not needed by selected cold-start design.

smallest_dynamic_validation: Start original vapp once under the permanent wrapper; create worker but keep original mode and do not take over output. Confirm both GUI input drivers and all original submit callbacks before replacing only those exact slots.

Instrument wrapper counters with pass-through only; verify stock display, physical/utouch decoding, framebuffer poll, key3 and cloud controls still function. This does not validate the mode transition yet.

At released contacts request transition; acknowledge closed in-flight callbacks, block stock submit, observe queue drain, submit owned custom frame and filter decoded GUI states while continuing to drain both rings.
Count new contacts only; verify stock UI has no hidden touch effects, original business remains alive, queue/staging are left native, and no second fb poll is opened.

Return with a verified stock redraw/source, released and drained contacts, and ordered callback acknowledgements. Repeat bounded round trips while observing stable FDs/subscriptions/heap and no Framework recreation.

If broker ownership/lifetime cannot be closed, the fallback is serialized Framework stop0x381a93a1 through its valid async/event context, wait for original main return and globalNULL, verify touch/renderer resources stop and scanout sources remain valid, restore signal2 disposition, then one original reentry and bounded return. That lifecycle path also remains unvalidated; do not kill or suspend an arbitrary task.
hardware_validation: Not performed by this review. Parent owns device operations and any final prototype choice.

input_transaction.transaction_candidate: GUI timer after original input drain takes broker mutex, then physical and virtual upper+4 in a fixed order, deduplicating equal uppers. No retained GUI heap pointers in worker. Under the upper locks verify GUI ring head==tail, original decoder caches released, physical released, AND custom worker own physical ring empty/pressed0. With GUI itself as the only consumer of its two subscribers, producer locks close pending-event replay across mode commit.
input_transaction.worker_old_events: Checking only two GUI rings does not show the custom worker ring is empty. input_transaction.new_contact_boundary: A contact first published after upper locks release belongs to the new owner, even if the physical GPIO/I2C state changed while gate/PAN was running. This is an explicit publication boundary, not proof of atomic touchscreen hardware state.
input_transaction.lock_limits: Native PAN normal successful path has no sem_wait/nanosleep dependency, but uses SMP spin/WFE and IRQ critical helpers, and critical leave can reschedule. Therefore no strict millisecond latency or no-scheduling claim. Holding upper locks delays publication during full-frame rotation. PAN failure logging and all possible IRQ dependencies are not globally audited.
input_transaction.review_scope: Static candidate only; parent owns dynamic lock-order, touch latency, and repeated hot-switch validation.
